headline: A 2021 law that delays automatic federal spending cuts and makes several technical changes to Medicare and Medicaid payment rules.
what_it_does: The law keeps Medicare exempt from automatic across-the-board spending cuts, called sequestration, until December 31, 2021. It applies certain modified payment limits to rural health clinics that temporarily enrolled in Medicare during the COVID-19 public health emergency or that applied to enroll by December 31, 2020. It also keeps higher Medicaid disproportionate-share hospital payments for public hospitals in California, even though future payment method changes are expected.

who_it_affects.how: Medicare spending is shielded from automatic sequestration cuts through the end of 2021.

who_it_affects.group: Rural health clinics that enrolled in Medicare during the COVID-19 emergency or applied by December 31, 2020
who_it_affects.how: These clinics are subject to certain modified Medicare payment limits.
They keep higher Medicaid disproportionate-share hospital payments under future payment method changes.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 14, 2021; the Medicare sequestration exemption runs through December 31, 2021.
